summary.headline: Styrenix Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 3.3% to INR84.5 crore on 10.8% margin, while Thailand remains loss-making and India capacity expansion is due by FY27 end.
summary.overview: Standalone total income rose 26.5% YoY to INR781 crore in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA up 3.3% to INR84.5 crore and PAT up 0.8% to INR51.2 crore on 43.4 KT volume. H1 standalone EBITDA grew 70% to INR286 crore (18.4% margin) on 82.4 KT. Consolidated Q2 EBITDA was INR75.6 crore (7.6% margin), with the gap to standalone attributed to the Thailand subsidiary. Management said ABS volumes recovered after a disrupted Q1, while GPPS volumes were deliberately reduced to avoid speculative styrene purchases; Phase 1 expansion remains on track for FY27 end.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated H1 FY27 total income / EBITDA / PAT
financial_highlights.value: INR2,009.8 crore / INR299.2 crore (14.9% margin) / INR161.5 crore

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Volumes rose significantly in Q2 after a disrupted Q1; management expects H2 ABS volumes in line with Q2 and says the business is back to normal. Current India capacity is running relatively full excluding Q1.

segments.name: HIPS (India)
segments.commentary: Roughly 35,000-40,000 tonnes capacity, with more than 70-80% of demand now OEM-driven (air conditioners, refrigerators, some packaging). Management expects HIPS volumes to stay at historical levels.

segments.name: GPPS (India)
segments.commentary: Volumes fell in Q2 as management chose not to serve speculative non-OEM demand; small OEM share. Management expects a modest improvement but will not return to historical levels without commitments.

segments.name: Thailand (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Consolidated-to-standalone gap implies a cash loss of about INR10 crore in Q2. Volumes flat, with 40-50% of sales to China, 20-25% to Thailand and the balance to Japan, Vietnam and others. Management guides to performance staying at last year's level for about two more years while cost-realignment projects run 1-1.5 years.

guidance_outlook: Phase 1 expansion (Nandesari rubber/ABS, Katol SAN, Moxi compounding) expected to commission by FY27 end; exact month (January or March) not committed, with a possible one-quarter lag.
Phase 2 ABS expansion in India stated as on schedule, with no delay and no specific completion timeline given.

Thailand performance expected to stay at last year's level for roughly 1.5-2 years, with significant improvement after cost realignment; volume growth expected over about two years and full utilisation in about three years.
Management assumes annualised gross margins and absolute spreads stay similar to the prior year; no formal volume guidance given.
Management expects a refrigeration-liner ABS grade (India imports roughly 30,000-40,000 tonnes; market 3.5-4 lakh tonnes) to be addressable once new capacity runs, with validation to follow start-up.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 expansion across Nandesari (rubber), Katol (SAN) and Moxi (compounding) targeted for commissioning by FY27 end; management says large part of new capacity should be utilised in FY28.
Phase 2 ABS expansion in India continues per original timeline, but no completion date given.
Thailand cost-realignment projects (rubber efficiency, manufacturing cost) started and expected to take 1-1.5 years.
Management indicated that once new capacity comes online, it expects to reach high utilisation quickly, though it did not commit to a volume ramp curve.
demand_pricing: Styrene monomer ranged about $1,300-1,700/tonne, recently around $1,600-1,650; management avoided speculative purchases given possible $200/tonne drops within about 30 days.
Most ABS and HIPS business is formula-linked; management says customers accepted raw-material cost pass-throughs and spreads were maintained.
Competitive intensity in India described as unchanged: Korean imports may be lower on freight, offset by lower utilisation in Taiwan, Thailand and China.
Management says it cannot quantify dumping (import data unavailable after March) but believes it exists; says import substitution preference remains.
Thailand: specialty product mix with no commodity ABS grades; some auto business lost on revalidation (a few hundred tonnes per year); China market share broadly maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Are there ABS grades imported into India that the company cannot yet produce, and is the new capacity addressing them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management highlighted refrigeration-liner ABS, with imports of about 30,000-40,000 tonnes out of a 3.5-4 lakh tonne market, which only Thailand technology and the new Indian capacity can address; validation follows start-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Thailand not showing gradual recovery and what is the trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost improvement requires projects of 1-1.5 years, so no gradual quarterly gains; management expects the business to remain flat for about two years, with product rebalancing and revalidation losses, and believes Q2 is the lowest quarterly volume base.

qa_highlights.question: Will GPPS volumes return in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: HIPS volumes are expected at historical levels; GPPS should improve modestly as non-OEM demand stabilises, but not back to historical levels unless the company is comfortable taking speculative raw-material positions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 standalone per-kg performance sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is fairly normalised for ABS and that annualised performance should be in line with the current quarter, excluding the lower GPPS volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected first-year utilisation levels for the new ABS plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward guidance, saying it could sell roughly 2,000-3,000 tonnes more ABS easily, but 4,000-5,000 tonnes immediately has not been worked on.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Thailand EBITDA per tonne been targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify EBITDA per tonne, saying the aim is to make Thailand structurally profitable on an annualised basis even at current volumes.

risks_watch: Thailand losses persist for roughly two more years; cost-realignment delivery and the timing of new product approvals are key.
Styrene monomer volatility (about $1,300-1,700/tonne) and speculative purchase risk, which led to lower GPPS volumes in Q2.
Phase 1 commissioning timing (FY27 end, potentially slipping by about a quarter) and the slow ramp-up of new capacity.
Competition from a third Indian ABS entrant and possible Chinese dumping, with import data unavailable since March.
Revalidation of automotive customers in Thailand; some auto business has been lost or shrunk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India ABS and HIPS demand and on the expansion schedule, but cautious and evasive on Thailand timelines and on GPPS volumes; management repeatedly declined to give volume or EBITDA-per-tonne guidance.
